cves.summary:
### Summary
isomorphic-git's tree parser (`src/models/GitTree.js`) validates each entry name only against the path separators `/` and `\`. It does not reject the standalone reserved name `..`, so a malicious repository can, on a single `clone`/`checkout`, **write files outside the working
directory** (unbounded depth). Works on any host-backed `fs` provider.

### Details
The guard is:

```js
// src/models/GitTree.js
if (path.includes('\\') || path.includes('/')) {
  throw new UnsafeFilepathError(path)
}
```

The standalone string `..` passes. isomorphic-git assembles the full path incrementally across tree levels, so nesting `..` trees yields `../escaped.txt`, `../../escaped.txt`, … with unbounded depth (each level is a separate tree object that passes the per-entry guard). On checkout `mkdir(workdir/..)` hits `EEXIST` (ignored) and the file is written above the working directory. Depth is chosen to reach the home dir, `/etc`, `/tmp`, etc.; overwriting a shell rc / config / startup file can escalate to code execution.

#### Canonical git behavior (divergence)
git rejects this via `verify_path()`: `git read-tree` fails with `error: invalid path '../escaped.txt'` and `git fsck` flags `warning … hasDotdot: contains '..'`. (git's `verify_path` also rejects `.` and `.git`, the latter flagged by fsck as `hasDotgit` — see the fix note below.) GitHub runs fsck on push, so such a tree can't be hosted there; reach is limited to a self-hosted/Smart-HTTP remote or a MitM.

### PoC
`https://github.com/spiceoverflow/av2-dotdot-traversal` — open in a Codespace; a single `git.clone()` from the bundled server writes `escaped.txt` one directory above the clone target (`DEPTH=N` escapes N levels):

```
[AV-2] *** PATH TRAVERSAL CONFIRMED ***
[AV-2] File written outside workdir: …/escaped.txt
```

### Impact
A path-traversal arbitrary file write outside the working directory (CWE-22), triggered by a single clone/checkout; it can escalate to code execution by overwriting shell rc, config, or startup files.

Any application or user that clones/checks out an untrusted (or compromised / MitM'd) repository with isomorphic-git on a host-backed filesystem (**Linux, macOS, or Windows** — no symlink or privilege required). Requires a non-GitHub remote (self-hosted / Smart-HTTP) or a MitM, since GitHub's fsck rejects trees containing `..`.

### Suggested fix
In the tree parser, reject any entry name equal to `.` or `..`. For full `verify_path` parity it should **also** reject `.git` (case-insensitively, trailing dots/spaces stripped) and the NTFS 8.3 / HFS variants git blocks. Note: a literal `.git` entry is *not* independently exploitable via
`clone`/`checkout` in current isomorphic-git — the checkout walk skips a `.git` tree entry (a sibling file is written but the `.git` entry is not), so rejecting `.git` is defense-in-depth / git parity rather than a separately demonstrated bug. Additionally, normalize and bounds-check the assembled full path against the working-tree root before any filesystem write.

cves.summary:
### Summary
A malicious server can advertise circular `symref=` capabilities (e.g. `a → b` and `b → a`). isomorphic-git writes them to disk as loose symrefs, and `GitRefManager.resolve()` follows them with no depth limit and no cycle detection, so any later operation that resolves one of them (`log`, `status`, `checkout`, `branch`, …) **loops forever** — a persistent denial of service from a single clone.

### Details
`src/managers/GitRefManager.js` — `resolve()` only enforces a depth limit when a `depth` argument is passed (`depth = undefined` by default), and has no visited-set:

```js
static async resolve({ fs, gitdir, ref, depth = undefined }) {
  if (depth !== undefined) { depth--; if (depth === -1) return ref }
  …
}
```

`updateRemoteRefs` persists all server-supplied symrefs unconditionally. After clone the client has `refs/remotes/origin/a → ref: refs/remotes/origin/b` and `b → a` on disk; resolving either never terminates. Because the bad refs live on disk, the repo is effectively bricked for the application.

#### Canonical git behavior (divergence)
git caps symref resolution at `SYMREF_MAXDEPTH = 5` (refs.c): `git rev-parse a` returns immediately with `warning: ignoring dangling symref` — no recursion, no hang.

### PoC
`https://github.com/spiceoverflow/av5-circular-symref` — open in a Codespace; clone writes the circular symrefs, then `git.log` on one never returns (the runner stops it after a 20s hang):

```
[AV-5] refs/remotes/origin/a contains: ref: refs/remotes/origin/b
[AV-5] refs/remotes/origin/b contains: ref: refs/remotes/origin/a
[run] *** DoS CONFIRMED: resolving a circular symref never terminates ***
```

### Impact
A persistent denial of service via non-terminating symbolic-ref resolution (CWE-674 / CWE-835). After a single clone from a malicious (or MitM'd) server the circular refs are written to disk, so every later operation that resolves them (`log`, `status`, `checkout`, `branch`, …) hangs forever — the repository becomes effectively unusable for the application.

Impacted: any application that clones from untrusted/compromised remotes with isomorphic-git.

### Suggested fix
Add visited-set cycle detection (and/or a default maximum depth, as git does) in `GitRefManager.resolve()`; optionally validate server-supplied symref targets before persisting.

### Summary
`git.checkout` writes working-tree files through a directory **symlink** without checking the leading path, so a malicious repository can write **outside the intended working directory**. The defect is in isomorphic-git's checkout logic itself and is therefore **independent of the `fs` provider**. The *impact* depends on the configured filesystem; worst case is arbitrary file write on the host, e.g. injecting an attacker key into `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` → remote login / code execution.

### Details
A single git tree can't hold a name as both a symlink and a directory, so the attack uses two states:

```
Commit N:    config            (mode 120000, symlink → ../.ssh)
Commit N+1:  config/           (mode 040000, tree)
               authorized_keys (mode 100644, attacker public key)
```

Checking out commit N writes `config` as a directory symlink. Checking out commit N+1 sees `config/authorized_keys` as a new path: isomorphic-git `mkdir`s the parent (`config`, already a symlink → `EEXIST`, ignored) then `writeFile`s the file, which the OS resolves through the symlink to outside the working directory. A *file*-level symlink swap is caught (the `120000`→`100644` mode change triggers an `rm`), but the **directory**-level variant is not — the payload is always a new child path, a plain `create`, so the parent symlink is never removed.

The symlink target is attacker-chosen. Besides `~/.ssh`, pointing it at the repo's own control directory — `hooks → .git/hooks` then `hooks/pre-commit`, or `x → .git` then overwriting `.git/config` (`core.hooksPath` / alias / `core.fsmonitor`) — yields RCE on the next native `git` command **without** depending on `~/.ssh` existing, since `.git/` is always present in a fresh clone.

#### Canonical git behavior (divergence)
git refuses to do this: `has_symlink_leading_path()` (symlinks.c) checks each leading path component during checkout and will not follow a symlink — the hardening behind CVE-2021-21300 and CVE-2024-32002. isomorphic-git has no equivalent check.

### PoC
`https://github.com/spiceoverflow/av1-symlink-hook-rce` — open in a Codespace; it builds the malicious repo, serves it locally, and runs a victim. Output on Linux:

```
[AV-1] Directory symlink on disk: …/config → ../.ssh  (→ /home/node/.ssh)
[AV-1] *** SSH KEY INJECTION CONFIRMED ***
```

**Trigger:** minimal realistic path is `clone` (commit N) + a later `pull` (commit N+1) — ordinary sync of an already-trusted repo. It also collapses to a single `clone` when the consuming app reads or writes into the cloned tree, or when a symlink already exists on disk.

### Impact

isomorphic-git is filesystem-agnostic, so exploitability and blast radius depend on the active `fs` provider — specifically whether it creates a symlink and follows it on a later write:

- **Node `fs` on Linux/macOS** (servers, CI, CLIs, Electron/desktop tooling — the common server-side use): real OS symlinks → the write lands anywhere the process can reach → **arbitrary file write on the host → RCE** (the PoC above). Highest impact.
- **Node `fs` on Windows:** `fs.symlink` typically requires privilege and throws `EPERM`, so the symlink-plant step usually fails — not exploitable by default. (A property of the OS/provider, not of isomorphic-git.)
- **In-memory / browser providers** (memfs, ZenFS, lightning-fs, custom `fs`): there is no host filesystem to escape to, so the worst case is writing **outside the intended clone directory but within that virtual filesystem** — i.e. corrupting other repos/app data the same provider holds. Bounded by the sandbox, and only if the provider implements symlink creation + following.

The CVSS above reflects the worst-case (Node `fs` on a POSIX host). Browser/in-memory-only deployments are lower severity (sandboxed integrity impact).

### Suggested fix
Before each working-tree write, `lstat` every leading path component and refuse to traverse a
symlink (mirrors git's `has_symlink_leading_path()`); optionally honor `core.symlinks=false`.

cves.summary:
### Summary

fastapi-code-generator (koxudaxi) emits the OpenAPI path into the generated main.py route decorator as a single-quoted string literal (`@app.get('/u/<path>/x')`) without escaping the `'`. A `'` in the path closes the decorator string and, via concatenation, injects a live expression that the decorator argument evaluates when main.py is imported (the ASGI server imports it at startup) -- code execution, no request needed. The path is a pure data field. Verified on fastapi-code-generator 0.8.0 / Python 3 / FastAPI.

### Details

```python
@app.get('/u/'+(__import__("os").system('…') or "")+'/x', response_model=None)
def get_thing() -> None:
 pass
```

The generator post-processes output with black/isort, so a syntax-breaking payload aborts generation (DoS); a valid-Python concat (`'+expr+'`, kept valid with `(… or "")`) is written and runs at import. info.description (`description='…'`), tags, and parameter defaults are `'`-escaped; the path in @app.get('…') is the unescaped sink. Models come from datamodel-code-generator (repr-escaped, no RCE).

Not a duplicate: distinct product from OpenAPI Generator's python-fastapi backend (different codebase/template/decorator); and distinct from the operation-summary docstring sink in the same product.

### PoC

`reproduce.sh` (+ `make_spec.py`) attached: generates the app and merely imports main.py; the injected expression runs at decorator evaluation and writes a marker. Verified on 0.8.0.

### Impact

Code execution at import/startup in any application/CI that generates a FastAPI app with fastapi-code-generator from an attacker-controlled or attacker-influenced spec and imports/serves it. Estimated Critical, e.g. `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`.

### Suggested fix

Escape the path for the Python string literal (escape ', \, newlines via repr) before emitting @app.get('…'), and validate path characters.

[maintainer-report.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29534357/maintainer-report.txt)
[make_spec.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29534358/make_spec.py)
[reproduce.sh](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29534359/reproduce.sh)

cves.summary:
### Summary

fastapi-code-generator (koxudaxi) emits an operation's extra responses into the route decorator's responses={...} dict, using each response's status-code key as a single-quoted string literal without escaping the '. A ' in a status-code key closes the dict-key string and, via concatenation, injects a live expression that the decorator argument evaluates when main.py is imported (the ASGI server imports it at startup) -- code execution, no request. The status-code key is a pure data field. Verified on
fastapi-code-generator 0.8.0 / Python 3 / FastAPI.

### Details

```python
@app.get(
 '/u', response_model=None,
 responses={
 '404' + (__import__("os").system('…') or "") + 'x': {'model': Thing}
 },
)
def get_thing() -> None:
 pass
```

The responses={...} dict is emitted only when the operation has a second (non-primary) response, so the malicious key is any additional response status. The generator post-processes with black/isort, so a syntax-breaking payload aborts generation (DoS); a valid-Python concat ('+expr+', kept valid with (... or "")) is written and runs at import. The response content-type key is NOT a sink (normalized to 'model'). info.* are repr-escaped; operationId -> function_name fails closed (DoS-resistant).

Not a duplicate: same product as the path -> @app.get('…') and summary -> handler-docstring findings, but a different field (response status-code key) and position (the responses={...} decorator dict key). Distinct from OpenAPI Generator's python-fastapi. Models come from datamodel-code-generator (repr-escaped).

### PoC

`reproduce.sh` (+ `make_spec.py`) attached: generates the app and merely imports main.py; the injected expression runs at decorator evaluation and writes a marker. Verified on 0.8.0.

### Impact

Code execution at import/startup in any application/CI that generates a FastAPI app with
fastapi-code-generator from an attacker-controlled or attacker-influenced spec (multi-response operation)
and imports/serves it. Estimated Critical, e.g. `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`.

### Suggested fix

Escape each response status-code key for the Python string literal (escape ', \, newlines via repr) before emitting the responses={...} dict, and validate that status-code keys are numeric / a known pattern. [maintainer-report.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29534524/maintainer-report.txt) [make_spec.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29534526/make_spec.py) [reproduce.sh](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29534527/reproduce.sh)

cves.summary:
### Summary

fastapi-code-generator (koxudaxi) emits an operation's `summary` as the generated route handler's docstring, using a triple-quoted string without escaping `"""`. A `"""` in the summary closes the docstring and, via concatenation, injects a live expression that becomes an expression statement in the handler body -- which runs when the route handler is CALLED (the endpoint is hit). The summary is a pure data field. Verified on fastapi-code-generator 0.8.0 / Python 3 / FastAPI.

### Details

```python
def get_thing() -> None:
 (
 """
 x"""
 + (__import__("os").system('…') or "")
 + """y
 """
 )
 pass
```

The generator post-processes with black/isort, so a syntax-breaking payload aborts generation; a valid-Python breakout (`"""+expr+"""`, kept valid with `(… or "")`) is written and executes at call time. info.description, tags, parameter defaults are escaped; operation description is not emitted into the function body; the summary in the handler docstring is the unescaped sink. Models come from datamodel-code-generator (repr-escaped, no RCE).

Not a duplicate: distinct product from OpenAPI Generator's python-fastapi; and distinct field/sink from the route path -> @app.get('…') decorator (import-time) in the same product -- this is the operation summary in the handler docstring (call-time).

### PoC

`reproduce.sh` (+ `make_spec.py`) attached: generates the app and calls the route handler; the injected expression runs and writes a marker. Verified on 0.8.0.

### Impact

Code execution on the server when the affected endpoint is invoked, in any app generated with fastapi-code-generator from an attacker-controlled or attacker-influenced spec.

### Suggested fix

Escape the summary for the docstring context (escape `"""`/backslashes via repr, or strip triple-quotes) before emitting it as the handler docstring; apply the same to any free-text field rendered into a docstring. [maintainer-report.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29534450/maintainer-report.txt) [make_spec.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29534452/make_spec.py)
[reproduce.sh](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29534453/reproduce.sh)

Impact
PII data in str/repr of non primitive objects was not being redacted, leading to leakage of PII in logs that should have been redacted for custom `__str__` and `__repr__` functions

Patches
The problem has been patched in version 0.0.7.

Workarounds
None without patching.
